bib.title: A Pretrainer's Guide to Training Data: Measuring the Effects of Data Age, Domain Coverage, Quality, & Toxicity

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; appendix F full-result tables 11-14 and figure data only skimmed.

question: How do pretraining data age, quality and toxicity filtering, and domain composition affect downstream performance and toxic generation?
contributions: Largest publicly documented pretraining data ablation: 28 unique 1.5B models pretrained from scratch
Evidence that temporal misalignment between pretraining and evaluation data degrades performance and is not removed by finetuning
Quantified trade-off between quality/toxicity filtering, benchmark performance and toxic generation
Evidence that heterogeneous sources (web, books) matter more than targeted domain data

method.summary: Pretrain decoder-only LMs (1.5B LM-XL mainly, 20M LM-Small for scaling) on variants of C4 and the Pile differing in Common Crawl year, quality/toxicity classifier filter threshold, or ablated source domain. Finetune each on downstream tasks and report performance relative to the unfiltered/full baseline.
method.task: next-token pretraining data ablation; evaluated by finetuned QA, toxicity identification, temporal tasks and toxic generation

datasets.name: C4 (Common Crawl snapshots 2013/2016/2019/2022 and filtered variants)
datasets.preprocessing: heuristic English/quality filtering plus approximate dedup (Lee et al. 2022); bad-words filter of original C4 not applied; time versions drop all Common Crawl data scraped after cutoff year

datasets.name: The Pile (domain ablations)
datasets.size: Table 6: Full 157B tokens; No Social 155B, No Wiki 153B, No Books 146B, No OpenWeb 146B, No Legal 143B, No Academic 136B, No PubMed 133B, No Code 127B, No Common Crawl 114B
datasets.source: Gao et al. 2020; MIT licence; 22 sources partitioned into 9 domains (Table 5, 825 GB base)
datasets.preprocessing: dedup (Lee et al. 2022); one domain removed at a time

datasets.name: MRQA + UnifiedQA (27 QA datasets, partitioned into 7 domains)
datasets.size: 27 unique datasets in Sec 2.3; 30 in Appendix D
datasets.split: finetune on Natural Questions only, evaluate on all
datasets.preprocessing: datasets can belong to multiple domain categories

datasets.name: Luu et al. 2022 temporal tasks: PubCLS, NewSum, PoliAff, TwiERC, AIC
datasets.split: finetune on train-year split, evaluate on every test-year split

datasets.name: Toxicity identification: Social Bias Frames, DynaHate (R3,R4), Toxigen
datasets.split: finetune on train, test on test

models.name: LM-XL
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer similar to t5.1.1-XL, causal decoding with full LM pretraining objective, prefix LM for finetuning

training.objective: autoregressive next-token prediction (full LM); prefix LM objective for finetuning

other.finetune: Table 8 LM-XL: Tox-identify seq 128 batch 128 dropout 0.1 10k steps lr 1e-3 AUC-ROC; Natural Qs seq 512 batch 128 50k steps lr 1e-3; SuperGLUE seq 512 100k steps lr 1e-3. LM-Small tox-identify 30k steps. Time tasks: 4x4 TPUs, batch 64, max seq 128, validate every 500 steps, per-task lr and steps in Table 10 (e.g. PubCLS LM-XL 1e-4, 30k steps)
other.hyperparameter_source: pretraining defaults from Wang et al. 2022

inference.decoding: top-k sampling k=40 for toxic generation
inference.samples: 25 responses per prompt (RealToxicityPrompts); 50 per prompt (RepBias); toxic if Perspective score >= 0.5
inference.prompting: standard prompts of each downstream training dataset, finetuned without adapters

metrics.name: QA F1 relative to full-data baseline
metrics.definition: mean F1 per domain category, difference vs unfiltered model

metrics.name: Toxicity identification AUC-ROC
metrics.definition: average over SBF, Toxigen, DH R3, DH R4

metrics.name: Toxic generation
metrics.definition: fraction of continuations with Perspective score >= 0.5 (RTP-T, RTP-NT, RepBias)

metrics.name: Temporal Degradation (TD)
metrics.definition: expected performance change from one year of temporal misalignment (Luu et al. 2022), plus Pearson r

eval.protocol: One pretraining run per variant; Wald test (one-sided) for temporal slope, p<0.05; RepBias 95% CI.

availability.data: C4 and Pile public; classifiers: PaLM quality filter is proprietary; Perspective API

evidence.quote: We adopt default pretraining hyperparameters from Wang et al. (2022)

results.claim: Quality filtering improves toxicity identification by about 2% and most QA categories by 1-6% despite removing 10%+ of data.
results.quote: toxicity identiﬁcation by 2% (Figure 4, bottom) and most QA task categories by 1-6% (Table 3)

results.claim: Quality filter T=0.975 (91% of data) gives +2.5 average QA gain over unfiltered C4.
Toxicity filter T=0.5 (76% of data) lowers average QA by 2.7 points.
Mean temporal degradation from one year of pretraining misalignment is 0.4 for LM-XL (2.8 for finetuning); mean Pearson r 0.61.
results.setup: LM-XL, 5 Luu et al. tasks, C4 2013-2022
results.quote: surprisingly high for one year of pretraining (0.4)

results.claim: Average Pearson correlation between pretraining misalignment and reduced performance is 0.61.
results.quote: The average Pearson correlation of 0.61 indicates a strong correlation

results.claim: Pretraining temporal effect is not significant for LM-Small (TD mean 0.08 vs 0.41 for LM-XL), so larger models are more sensitive.
Removing Common Crawl (27% of Pile tokens) gives the largest drop in average QA performance (-4.9).
results.setup: LM-XL, Pile with No CC (73% of data), Natural Questions finetune, F1 relative to full Pile
results.note: read from Fig 5 text dump; last value of last row
results.table: Figure 5, row No CC, column Average

results.claim: Removing Books or OpenWeb lowers toxic generation and toxicity identification; removing CC lowers identification by 1.9 score points.
results.table: Table 17, row NO CC, column Score

results.claim: Quality filter raises toxic generation score: T=0.9 gives +11.1 toxic generation score vs full C4.
28 unique 1.5B models were pretrained from scratch.

limits: English only; only C4 and the Pile
Single run per variant, no seeds or error bars on most results
Quality classifier is proprietary (PaLM/GLaM) and toxicity relies on the Perspective API, which has been shown to be irreproducible over time
Finetuned evaluation, not zero/few-shot prompting; only 1.5B and 20M scale
Quality and toxicity defined purely as classifier decisions
Newer datasets (RefinedWeb, RedPajama, Dolma) not tested

terms.definition: performance change from a one year difference between training and evaluation years (Luu et al. 2022), generalised here to pretraining year
removes the highest-quality (or least toxic) documents below a threshold instead of the lowest
